config.mask_reason: 3' primer-binding tail (AAAGAAACAACAACAACAAC): reactivities ~1e-4, no structural information. Stored as numbers in the RDAT, set to NaN here.

report_notes.construct: P4-P6 domain of the Tetrahymena group I intron (RDAT NAME: 'P4-P6 domain, Tetrahymena ribozyme'), mutate-and-map experiment (DMS, MaP readout); only the wild-type row is used.
report_notes.region: R = 100-140 (RDAT numbering) contains the 5' arms of P4 (107-112) and P5 (116-121) and the start of P5a (127-138); their partners lie at 200-214 and 180-195, i.e. outside small 5'-anchored windows. This mimics the mRNA use case (5'-anchored window growing toward 3').
data_caveats: Positions 90-92 have reactivity exactly 0 and 93-99 are near 0 (possible low read coverage near the 5' end); they lie outside R and do not enter E.
Low DMS signal in the first positions of R (100-103) is part of E; it may reflect coverage rather than structure.
limitations: P4-P6 is not an mRNA: the test validates the method, but choosing a window for mRNAs requires mRNA probing data.
P4-P6 forms an extensive Mg2+-dependent tertiary structure (A-rich bulge, tetraloop/receptor), which none of the models capture.

bootstrap.scheme: paired circular block bootstrap over positions of R; E members kept

report_notes.construct: Hox A9 mRNA 5' UTR (1266 nt), 1M7 SHAPE, ligation-based readout (ligSHAPE), PAGE-purified RNA (row 1 of 2; row 2 is non-PAGE). Data were normalised over a 350-nt window (file comment).
report_notes.region: R = 1-100: the 5' end of the UTR. The region of interest is the 5'-most stretch with data (uniform rule across datasets: first 50 nt, 100 nt for the 1266-nt HOXA9 UTR), with 5'-anchored windows mimicking the mRNA use case.
data_caveats: RNA was heat-denatured, then folded at 37 °C for 20 min with 10 mM MgCl2; the annotated probing temperature is 24 °C. RNAfold folds at the annotated 24 °C.
SHAPE reagent: all four nucleotides enter E.
Window grid step is 50 nt because MXfold2 needs ~100 s per full-length fold.
limitations: HOXA9 data are normalised SHAPE reactivities with some negative values; Spearman ρ is unaffected by the normalisation but the noise floor is not modelled.

report_notes.construct: Bovine rotavirus A strain RF, genome segment 11 (NSP5/NSP6 mRNA), full-length in vitro T7 transcript (667 nt in the RASP reference). In vitro DMS-MaPseq, 0.5% (v/v) DMS ('50mM' in the RASP track name), no NSP2. Coria et al. 2022 NAR 50:10078.

data_caveats: Conditions from the paper's Methods (not from the file): refolded 65 °C 5 min then slow cooling; probed at 37 °C for 1 min in 5 mM HEPES-Na pH 7.5, 0.5 mM MgCl2, 100 mM NaCl, ~200 mM bicine pH 8.0.
Track values are RASP's 'raw' DMS-MaPseq reactivities; normalisation does not matter for Spearman correlation.
Data come from RASP v2 (genome-coordinate bigWig); the sequence is taken from RASP's reference FASTA for segment RFS11.
limitations: Low Mg2+ (0.5 mM) differs from the 10 mM Mg2+ RMDB datasets; none of the models has a Mg2+ term.
A viral mRNA segment, not a cellular 5' UTR.

Cheng et al. 2022 NAR 50:12001. Numbering = genome coordinate.

Of the equilibrium transcript lengths in RASP (135, 160, 220 nt) the longest was chosen, so the window test has the most room.
limitations: Experimental conditions are partly unknown (see Data caveats).
BzCN SHAPE-seq: all four nucleotides are evaluated.
